title: Thermal threshold latency surge — hosted API P1 investigation
body:
Summary:
During the 2027-04-20 morning window (UTC), the hosted API experienced a P1-level latency surge for approximately 23 minutes, affecting ~18% of requests served by one GPU cluster pool in us-west-2. Client-visible symptom: 95th percentile tail latency for text-generation increased from ~280ms to ~3.2s; a small but persistent 5xx uptick (mostly 503) accompanied the spike as some requests timed out at the edge.

High level impact:
- Duration: ~23 minutes (2027-04-20T09:12Z - 09:35Z)
- Scope: subset of requests routed to gpu-pool-03 (us-west-2) serving midsize models (7B-13B variants)
- Customer impact: degraded tail latency and an increase in user-facing timeouts; no data loss.
- Severity: P1 (latency SLO breach, user-facing)

Immediate detection and response:
- Alert: automated latency SLO alert fired at 09:13Z (oncall SRE Pager duty -> page to "sre-hosted-api").
- Pager escalations: primary on-call (Owen) acked at 09:13, triage called for platform lead and infra.
- Initial mitigation: traffic steering to warm fallback pool (gpu-pool-02) was triggered by runbook step at 09:17Z but only partially effective due to sticky routing for persistent sessions. Full fallback achieved at 09:25Z after manual route override.

Timeline (collected from logs, oncall chat, and kernel metrics):
- 09:11:27Z - Small increase in kernel thermal warnings on nodes gce-usw2-gpu-3* (fan speed events).
- 09:12:48Z - Edge latency alert begins to trend up; SRE monitor triggers SLO alert at 09:13:09Z.
- 09:13:20Z - First 503 spike observed at edge LB; symptom: backend connection resets.
- 09:14:30Z - Oncall investigates and opens SRE-1772; initial hypothesis: software regression in runtime scheduling.
- 09:15:12Z - Infra alerted: GPU driver logs show repeated GPU clock downscaling events correlated with high package temperatures.
- 09:16:40Z - Autoscaler reports transient capacity pressure; new pods scheduled onto same rack causing heat concentration.
- 09:17:05Z - Runbook automated steering recommended moving traffic; partial rollout to gpu-pool-02 starts.
- 09:20:50Z - Persistent sessions continue to hit affected hosts; manual route override started at 09:22Z.
- 09:24:07Z - Cooling system telemetry shows fan RPMs on node A03 drop intermittently; one node shows a failing fan alarm at 09:23:55Z.
- 09:25:01Z - Manual routing fully diverted traffic; latencies begin to fall.
- 09:28:30Z - 95th percentile back to ~320ms; 503s largely resolved by 09:30Z.
- 09:35:00Z - Incident declared mitigated, begin post-incident data collection.

Root cause (synthesis):
We attribute the incident to a confluence of three issues:
1) A hardware degradation (failing GPU fan) on node gce-usw2-gpu-03A that caused sustained thermal pressure at the node level. The GPU driver responded by aggressive clock-throttling to protect silicon, increasing inference latency.
2) The cluster autoscaler scheduled additional latency-sensitive pods onto the same rack to satisfy a transient capacity signal; this increased local thermal density and exacerbated throttling. Autoscaler placement constraints did not account for fan-health or recent thermal history.
3) Runbook automation did steer traffic to fallback pools, but session affinity and a late manual override meant mitigation was slower than necessary for tail-sensitive workloads.

Evidence and signals:
- GPU driver logs (nvml) show repeated power/clock-change events (clock downscale from 1650MHz -> 600MHz) coincident with package_temp readings > 85C.
- Node telemetry shows fan RPM drop before temp spike; firmware event present (SEL log) indicating fan tachometer signal loss.
- Kubernetes scheduling events show 7 pods placed onto nodes in same rack between 09:10-09:16Z.
- Edge logs show TCP resets to the affected backends followed by 5xx responses until requests reached fallback hosts.
- Perf traces show increased token generation time on affected hosts (per-token latency bump).

Why this wasn't caught earlier (contributing factors):
- Thermal/fan health metric was not part of the placement constraints or autoscaler decision tree; only node CPU/GPU utilization and available memory were considered.
- Fan tachometer failure does not map to a hard "unhealthy" state in our infra healthchecks; it required manual firmware parsing to detect.
- Sticky session affinity at the LB (necessary for streaming sessions) meant steering automation took longer to reach 100% effectiveness.
- No prior threshold breach policy for package_temp over 80C sustained for >2 minutes existed as an automated trigger.

Mitigations applied during incident:
- Immediate: traffic diverted to warm fallback pool (gpu-pool-02) and manual route override to ensure sticky sessions were rebalanced (09:22Z - 09:25Z).
- Evacuated the failing node from rotation (cordon + drain) at 09:30Z.
- Infra forced a firmware-level fan cycle and scheduled a hardware replacement ticket with cloud provider (ticket: SRE-HW-904, created 09:36Z).
- Autoscaler placement constraints temporarily adjusted to prefer rack-spread for latency-sensitive pools (09:33Z).

Post-incident actions (short-term):
- Hardware replacement confirmed for node gce-usw2-gpu-03A; OEM replacement scheduled 2027-04-21.
- Re-enable autoscaler with stricter rack/spread constraints for hosted-api latency pools by 2027-04-22 (owner: Tomás).
- Patch routing automation to add faster fallback for sessions with long-lived affinity (owner: Owen, target 2027-04-24).

Runbook and monitoring changes (longer-term):
- Add a thermal-health signal to node readiness and to autoscaler decision inputs: include fan RPM, nvml package_temp, and recent clock-throttle counts as part of scheduling score.
- Create an automated anomaly that will proactively cordon nodes with "tachometer failure" in SEL logs and drain if pack_temp > 82C for >90s.
- Lower SLO alert threshold for 95th latency for streaming sessions (investigate alert noise tradeoffs).
- Add a dashboard panel and synthetic probe for per-host package_temp and clock-throttle events (owner: Marisol, dashboard: grafana:dash/hosted-api/latency-heatmap).

Runbook draft changes (text to be committed):
- New step: If 95th(latency) > 1.5s and provider node pack_temp >82C AND clock_throttle_count > 5 within 2m -> immediately cordon affected host(s), invoke "evacuate-latency-sensitive" job, and notify infra oncall.
- Add explicit "session affinity mitigation" step: if steering is partial after 3m, perform LB-level sticky-session override and mark for manual reconciliation.
- Add an autoscaler override knob: allow human operator to set "thermal-avoid" placements on a per-pool basis for 1h.

Action items (owners and dates):
- Tomás Iglesias: Update autoscaler placement algorithm to consider thermal health signals; rollout canary 2027-04-22.
- Marisol Vega: Create Grafana panels + synthetic tests for package_temp/clock-throttle + alert runbook; due 2027-04-23.
- Owen Park: Implement LB sticky-session override in automation + test; due 2027-04-24.
- Priya Menon: Add firmware-level SEL parsing into node-health exporter and create cordon-drain automation; due 2027-04-28.
- Aisha (owner): Follow-up with CSP for hardware RMA confirmation + file SRE-HW-904 close report; due 2027-04-22.

Postmortem notes and uncertainties (open questions):
- Why did fan RPM drop intermittently rather than fail hard? Hardware vendor to provide more logs.
- Did rack-level airflow play a role? Need datacenter-level cooling logs.
- Are there other nodes with similar degraded tachometer traces? Batch-scan required.

Lessons learned (operational):
- Treat thermal telemetry as first-class for latency-critical inference workloads. Hardware failures manifest as performance regressions (not just hard failures).
- Autoscaler should optimize for thermal spread in addition to utilization — co-locating many heavy pods onto one rack increases risk.
- Automation is valuable but we must bake in session-affinity semantics; fallback that ignores affinity can leave many sessions still hitting degraded backends.

Notes-to-self / oncall transcript highlights (raw):
- "09:16: "nvml throttling trace, temp spike + fan tach lost" (Tomás)
- "09:21: "partial steering — sticky sessions still hitting A03; initiating manual override" (Owen)
- "09:26: "latency falling after manual override; keep an eye for regression" (Marisol)
- quick wins: add temp -> cordon rule; make steering more aggressive for sessions >10s"

Severity classification and customer communications:
- Incident classified P1 due to SLO breach and customer-visible degradation.
- Customer-facing note: an incident summary and mitigation timeline will be posted to status.redwood.ai; technical root cause summary will be shared with immediate impacted accounts by CS (owner: Michael Chen) on 2027-04-22.

Appendix: Relevant logs and pointers
- nvml extracts (snippets): GPU A03 -> package_temp 86C -> clock-change events (09:12:50 - 09:25:00)
- K8s events: scheduling bursts to node group gce-usw2-rack-03 between 09:10-09:16
- Edge LB logs: tcp reset pattern -> 503s for backends A03:A05 range
- Jira: SRE-1772 (incident), SRE-HW-904 (hardware RMA)

Closing note:
This incident is an instructive example where hardware health and scheduler placement interact to create a user-visible performance event. Short-term mitigations worked, but we need to harden autoscaler and node health signals to prevent recurrence. Draft runbook edits above — please comment inline and we'll move to a final runbook commit in Confluence after owners confirm timelines.

END OF DRAFT
